meta.data: 5 axial FLAIR slices, MSD Task01, largest-tumor slice, tight box prompt
meta.heatmap: decoder attention map via forward hooks (simplified, NOT full TMME), 64x64 upsampled
meta.audit: cascading random re-init of weight matrices/kernels, 3 seeds, output->input
meta.primary_metric_note: SSIM was the pre-registered metric; switched to Spearman after results showed SSIM cannot discriminate for this heatmap resolution. See metric_decision_log for the full reasoning trail.

rules.v1_ssim_prereg: SSIM<=0.5 at decoder_full (fixed before results) - 0/5 passed
rules.v2_spearman_posthoc: Spearman<=0.3 at decoder_full (chosen after results) - 5/5 passed

metric_decision_log.what: pre-registered pass/fail rule, fixed BEFORE running the audit
metric_decision_log.rule: SSIM(heatmap A, heatmap B) <= 0.5 at the decoder_full randomization stage
metric_decision_log.reasoning: SSIM is a standard image-similarity metric; 0.5 was chosen as a demo cutoff before seeing any results.

metric_decision_log.what: result of applying the pre-registered rule
metric_decision_log.result: 0 of 5 cases passed. SSIM stayed between 0.50-0.61 at decoder_full across all cases and never dropped much further even at full-model randomization (0.40-0.51 at enc_full).

metric_decision_log.what: investigation: is SSIM actually measuring what we want here?
metric_decision_log.test: Compared heatmap A against a plain synthetic Gaussian blob centered on the box prompt (no model involved at all).
metric_decision_log.finding: The fake blob scored SSIM 0.37-0.70 against real heatmap A - statistically indistinguishable from how similar heatmap B (fully randomized model) scored against A (0.43-0.62). This means SSIM gives smooth/blurry maps a high baseline similarity almost regardless of content, because our heatmaps are only 64x64 upsampled to 512x512. SSIM is not a reliable discriminator for this heatmap resolution.

metric_decision_log.what: metric switch, made AFTER seeing the above result
metric_decision_log.new_rule: Spearman rank correlation(heatmap A, heatmap B) <= 0.3 at decoder_full
metric_decision_log.reasoning: Spearman checks whether bright/dark regions keep the same relative ranking, independent of blur/smoothness. It collapsed from 1.0 (control) to near 0 (-0.09 to 0.06) at decoder_full across all 5 cases, matching visual inspection of heatmap A vs B and matching the collapse in randomized-model Dice (0.90->0.05-0.13).
metric_decision_log.result: 5 of 5 cases pass under this rule.

metric_decision_log.text: Because this switch was made after observing results on these same 5 cases, the 0.3 threshold and the choice of Spearman are NOT independently validated. They are a defensible post-hoc correction, not a pre-registered test. A held-out case set would be needed to validate this rule properly. Additionally, the prompt-encoder (which embeds the box) was never randomized in any stage, so part of any remaining similarity may reflect the box location rather than learned weights.

caveats: 5 slices demonstrate the pipeline, they do not validate it
SSIM has a high floor on smooth heatmaps
MPRT is a necessary sanity check, not proof of faithfulness
Spearman-based pass rule is post-hoc, not independently validated
